extracted.intended_audience: science communicators, press officers, and PR professionals preparing press releases (especially for Dutch/small-language markets and wire distribution)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing science press releases to maximize pickup in newspapers (with emphasis on Dutch/small-language markets and wire translation/routing). Focuses on what elements increase the chance journalists will reproduce citation and methodological information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-attributed citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Embed the citation in the release lead (e.g., 'according to a study published today in Nature, ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because most science news items omit source attribution, releases that embed the citation in the lead increase the probability the citation survives into final copy. Best practice: put a clear, self-contained citation/attribution in the opening sentences so journalists who copy-paste the lead retain the source reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological summary in pre-canned form
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a 1–2 sentence methods summary in lay language at the top of the release, ready for direct copy-paste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A short, plain-language methods snippet placed near the top has higher survival in final news items than methods buried later in the release. Make it concise, non-technical, and copy-paste friendly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page-target awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor the release to the intended pickup page: give scientific detail for science-section pickup and foreground impact in plain language for general-news pickup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Releases targeted at science sections should include greater scientific detail; releases aimed at general pages should prioritize audience-impact framing. Ideally supply both versions or clearly mark which version suits which audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor-interview alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead should signal audience interest first (what makes the story interesting to readers), not scientific rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor interviews showed selection is driven more by perceived audience interest than methodological depth. Therefore craft the lead to answer 'why your readers should care' before emphasizing technical quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standalone interpretability
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases must be interpretable without a follow-up call to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because newsrooms cannot easily reach scientists for clarification, provide self-contained explanations, clear quotes, and necessary context so journalists can use the material without additional contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multilingual robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply a version in English (or otherwise suitable for wire translators) for small-language markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In markets like the Netherlands, pickups often occur via wire translation. Providing a pre-written English version appropriate for translators increases the chance of accurate and frequent reproduction across outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine-channel match
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure releases reach routine amplification channels (e.g., national press agency ANP) in publishable form to increase spread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dutch newspapers rely heavily on national agencies. Releases sent to or made available in a format usable by such agencies get amplified broadly; direct-to-newspaper distribution reaches fewer outlets. Tailor format and timing for the channel you want to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Include clear limitations in the release; doing so does not reduce uptake and may increase downstream caveat reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although omissions of limitations don't hurt pickup, subsequent literature finds that including limitations raises the chance that caveats are reproduced later without reducing uptake. Best practice: transparently state key limitations while keeping the lead audience-focused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pickup drivers: ease-of-publication, audience-interest signal, wire-channel routing
rubrics_metrics.description: Pickup is driven less by scientific quality and more by (i) ease-of-publication for journalists, (ii) an audience-interest signal in the lead, and (iii) correct wire-channel routing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design releases to be easy for journalists to publish (copy-paste friendly leads and pre-canned methods), to immediately communicate why readers should care, and to be distributed through the channels (e.g., press agencies, translator-ready English copy) that newsrooms use. Scientific richness is less predictive of pickup than these practical factors.
